subject: Deployment option recap & preliminary cost scenarios
summary: Post-demo follow-up that clarifies hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment economics for Acme. Includes a conservative cost model for 100M tokens/month and asks for expected sustained QPS and contract length preferences.
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment option recap & preliminary cost scenarios

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed on the call: 

Key takeaways from our conversation:
- Goal: integrate Redwood for inference powering Acme Assist (real-time assistance for technicians). Primary constraints are sub-150ms p95 latency, customer data residency in us-west, and predictable monthly spend.
- Expected steady-state: ~100M generated tokens/month (peak bursts up to 10x for short periods).
- Preference: low ops surface, but willing to consider Dedicated or Private if economics + SLAs justify it.

Deployment options (high-level):
1) Hosted API (Redwood-managed): lowest time-to-value, zero infra ops for you, pay-as-you-go per-token. Good for initial launch and variable burst patterns.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): reserved GPU pools with commit discounts — predictable throughput and lower unit cost at high sustained volume; Redwood handles runtime and SLA.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking or fully on-prem; required for regulated data and tight network controls. Higher upfront and ops cost.

Preliminary cost scenarios (ballpark, for discussion) — assumption: 100M generated tokens/month, typical 1:1 input:output token ratio for throughput math: 
- Hosted API: ~$0.0008 per generated token => ~ $80,000 / month. Includes autoscaling, multi-region fallback, and pay-for-what-you-use.
- Dedicated (1-year reserved commit): effective unit ~$0.00035–$0.0005 per generated token depending on commit level and utilization => roughly $35k–$50k / month equivalent if you maintain steady 100M tokens and use a 12-month commit. We can tighten numbers if you share a target commit (e.g., 100M/mo x 12 = 1.2B tokens).
- Private VPC / on-prem: one-time platform fee + infra. Example starting point: platform license ~$250k + infra (GPU fleet) + ops; equivalent monthly run rate depends heavily on utilization — at high utilization it can be competitive vs Dedicated but requires customer infra/ops.

Tradeoffs: Hosted gives fastest path and flexibility for spikes; Dedicated gives predictable unit economics and stronger latency SLOs for tail; Private gives max control/residency at the cost of ops and upfront commitment.

Next steps we suggest: 
1) Could you confirm whether Acme needs a hard limit on p95 latency (<150ms) versus a target?
2) Share a rough monthly commit preference (no commit / 6-mo / 12-mo / 24-mo) and whether CapEx is preferred over OpEx.
3) If helpful, we attached a simple cost model (RW-cost-model-acme.xlsx) that breaks down token math and shows per-scenario sensitivity at 50M/100M/250M tokens.

I’ll follow up with a focused Dedicated vs Hosted one-pager tailored to your desired commit length and an estimated timeline for a pilot.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: RW-cost-model-acme.xlsx (Excel), SOC2-Summary.pdf (PDF)

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment option recap & preliminary cost scenarios

Thanks Soojin — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick clarifying questions before we dig into the workbook: 

1) For Dedicated, what is the minimum commit you require to hit the $0.00035/token band? Is that a per-month commit or an annual commitment?
2) For Hosted, do you have a mechanism to cap spend during the spikes? We have a hard budget constraint in Q4.
3) For Private, can you ballpark what "platform license" covers vs a separate installer/ops handoff? We prefer minimal ongoing vendor dependencies if we do private.

Also — we have one procurement person on copy (procurement@acme.ai). I can loop in our Infra lead if we get to Private. For now, we want to validate whether Dedicated gives meaningful cost savings vs Hosted for the volumes above.

Best,
Elena
VP Product | Acme Robotics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment option recap & preliminary cost scenarios

Elena — answers inline and a quick sketch of what we'd propose for Acme: 

1) Dedicated commit bands: 
- $0.00035/token band assumes a 12-month committed volume >= 1.2B generated tokens (i.e., ~100M/month sustained). We price commits as an annualized commitment with monthly invoicing options.
- 6-month commits typically land in the $0.0004–$0.0005/token range for the same monthly volume because of shorter-term commitment.

2) Hosted spend caps and guardrails: 
- Yes — we can set hard spend limits at the account route level (alerts + hard cap). We also offer burst protection to gracefully degrade to a smaller model variant rather than exhaust budget. For Q4 we can set quota limits and a policy route for fallback to a cheaper model.

3) Private platform license details: 
- License covers the control plane software + 12 months of updates & enterprise support. It does not include the customer infra (GPUs, networking) or on-site professional services beyond 5 days. For hands-off private deployments we offer a managed on-prem option (add-on) that increases the platform fee but reduces your ops lift.

Proposed next deliverable: a 1-page pricing comparison that assumes your 100M tokens/mo baseline and shows: Hosted (no commit), Dedicated 12-mo commit (1.2B), Dedicated 24-mo commit (2.4B), and a private total-cost-of-ownership at 3 utilization scenarios (50%, 75%, 95%). That will let procurement make a apples-to-apples comparison.

If that sounds good, can you confirm whether procurement prefers quotes with or without tax & whether we should include an optional pilot seat (30-day pilot at reduced rate) in the packet?

I'll attach a quick exported snapshot from the cost model into the one-pager once I have your preference.

Thanks — will follow up with the one-pager by EOD.

— Soojin
